source:
I am Elise, lady to the Queen, servant all my life. They say I am mad with fever. But this is truth. Hear my final story, if you are able, if you care a whit, if you can know its significance.

I was barely more than a child myself when Simona was first let into the castle, a glowing vision of a girl dressed in a peasant's rags. Even then the head scullery maid ordered her hair be covered so she didn't attract 'attention'. In the end, it made no difference.

Simona was kind to me. This, I recall. I often helped the girl with her work as she braided the Queen's hair. After she was finished, Queen Astrid would beg her to stay, to tell stories. Simona had a way with stories. She never refused. And when King Alexander came to bed and woo Simona, who was she to refuse him, either?

Then there was the book. That horrid book... Simona brought it home. From where? Who gave it to her? I still don't know. Four days later, news of Queen Astrid's sudden death shocked the castle into mute horror, and Simona was quietly whisked away to the King's chambers. She was now the King's only lover. A low-born nobody with the power to rule nations.

The guards whispered of Queen Astrid's body: of how she died with her own nails lodged in her throat, the flesh torn, gone abruptly and thoroughly mad, her blood seeping through the keep tower's floor.

Simona came to me early one morning when it was still dark, inconsolably upset and without a light. "The book is cursed," She whispered to me in the darkness, her face wet with tears. "Elise, you don't understand. I was trapped in Elsinore for ever, for a thousand years or more. I saw every outcome I could, every possible version of this world, and it was all rotten. What could I do, Elise? What could I do? The book made me choose, and I chose to let Astrid rot with it all, so I could rule..."

She kissed me goodbye and pressed a coin into my hand. "I cannot hide from God," she said. "But I cannot stay in Elsinore. Tell no one where I went. Promise me, Elise."

And here I am, breaking that promise. I know Simona lives. What happened that insane week all those years ago? What will become of little Ophelia and Laertes, and my beloved husband I left behind? I will go to my grave not knowing.

Should my family ever read this, know this: I lived a far luckier life than any woman of my station ought to have enjoyed. But the luckiest thing in my world was always you.

我是伊莉丝，王后的侍女，一辈子都在服侍人。他们说我发烧烧疯了。但这些都是真的。请听听我最后的故事，只要你还能听，只要你还有一点在乎，只要你能明白它意味着什么。

西蒙娜初次获准进入城堡时，我自己也才刚过孩童的年纪。她穿着农家人的破衣烂衫，却美得光彩照人。那时，洗碗女仆的领班就命令她把头发遮起来，免得引来“注意”。到头来，这也没起什么作用。

西蒙娜待我很好。这一点，我记得。她为王后编头发时，我常常帮她做事。编完之后，阿斯特丽德王后总会央求她留下来讲故事。西蒙娜很会讲故事。她从不拒绝。而当亚历山大国王来向西蒙娜求欢、与她同床时，她又哪有资格拒绝他呢？

后来，那本书出现了。那本可怕的书……西蒙娜把它带回了家。从哪里来的？是谁给她的？我至今都不知道。四天后，阿斯特丽德王后猝死的消息让整个城堡陷入惊恐，鸦雀无声，而西蒙娜被悄悄带进了国王的寝宫。如今，她成了国王唯一的情人。一个出身卑微的无名之辈，却有了统治列国的权力。

卫兵们悄声议论着阿斯特丽德王后的尸体：她死时，自己的指甲还扎在喉咙里，皮肉被撕破；她突然彻底疯了，鲜血渗过了主堡塔楼的地板。

一天清晨，天还没亮，西蒙娜就来找我。她悲痛欲绝，也没带灯。“那本书受了诅咒，”她在黑暗中低声对我说，满脸都是泪。“伊莉丝，你不明白。我被永远困在埃尔西诺，困了一千年，甚至更久。我看遍了我能看到的每一种结局，这个世界每一种可能的模样，全都腐烂不堪。我能怎么办，伊莉丝？我能怎么办？那本书逼我选择，而我选择让阿斯特丽德和这一切一起腐烂，好让我掌权……”

她吻了我，向我道别，又把一枚钱币塞进我手里。“我躲不过上帝，”她说，“但我不能留在埃尔西诺。别告诉任何人我去了哪里。答应我，伊莉丝。”

而现在，我却在违背那个承诺。我知道西蒙娜还活着。多年前那个疯狂的星期里，究竟发生了什么？年幼的奥菲莉娅和雷欧提斯，还有我留下的心爱丈夫，往后会怎样？我到死都不会知道。

如果我的家人有一天读到这些，请记住：我这一生的幸运，远远超过了像我这样身份的女人所能奢望的。但在我的世界里，最幸运的事，始终是有你们。

source:
May 2, MDXXXV

Tonight my husband seemed distressed. At first I thought he was missing our son, gone to Wittenberg. But... as the night progressed, he seemed to grow old before my eyes. He seemed... broken, somehow. When the second course was served, he collapsed while raising a toast—ironically, a toast to our health. I took him on my shoulders and bore him out of the great hall and up to his bedroom myself. 

As I lay him down in his bed, I noticed tears in his eyes. I tried to comfort him by kissing his forehead, but he pushed me away. "You will betray me," he rasped. "You will always betray me. Every time. You cannot do otherwise." 

He collapsed into something like sleep, then, and would not answer my questions.

When I returned to the party, our guests were concerned, but Claudius stepped in to assure them. "Everything's all right!" he boomed, in his loudest, most regal voice. "Everyone—Drink more! Don't take your health for granted!"

Then he turned and offered me his hand. "Now. I think a dance with the Queen will restore some life to this party. Don't you?" he said, smiling at me. It was as though I were the only woman in the whole world. In all my time married to Hamlet, he never once looked at me like that.

That evening, when all the guests had gone to bed, I found myself outside my bedroom door, saying my goodnights to Claudius.

"I don't want to go to bed," I told him, laughing. "I want the night to continue. Stop the dawn!"

"As you wish, my Queen," he said, and kissed me.

I was surprised at first. And yet—I wasn't. 

I kissed him back. He pulled my bedroom door shut behind him.

Surely I, too, deserve some happiness in this world that has been so cruel to me.

Don't I?

MDXXXV年5月2日

今晚，丈夫似乎心神不宁。起初，我以为他在想念去了威登堡的儿子。但……随着夜色渐深，他仿佛在我眼前衰老了。他看起来……像是被什么击垮了。第二道菜端上来时，他正举杯祝酒，却倒了下去——讽刺的是，他祝的正是我们身体安康。我把他扛在肩上，亲自将他带出大厅，送上楼送进他的卧室。 

把他放到床上时，我发现他眼里有泪。我吻了吻他的额头，想安慰他，他却推开了我。“你会背叛我，”他声音嘶哑地说，“你永远都会背叛我。每一次。你做不到别的。” 

随后，他陷入了像是睡眠的状态，不再回答我的问题。

我回到宴会上时，宾客们都很担心，克劳狄斯却站出来安抚他们。“一切都好！”他用最洪亮、最有王者威严的声音说道，“各位——再多喝些！别把身体安康当成理所当然！”

接着，他转身向我伸出手。“来吧。我想，与王后共舞一曲，会让这场宴会重新热闹起来。你说呢？”他说着，朝我微笑。仿佛我是全世界唯一的女人。嫁给哈姆雷特这么久，他从未这样看过我，哪怕一次。

那晚，宾客们都去睡了，我站在自己的卧室门外，正向克劳狄斯道晚安。

“我不想睡，”我笑着对他说，“我想让这一夜继续下去。别让天亮！”

“遵命，我的王后。”他说，然后吻了我。

起初我很惊讶。然而——我又并不惊讶。 

我回吻了他。他随手关上了身后的卧室门。

这个世界对我如此残酷，我当然也该得到一些幸福。

难道不是吗？

source:
Again... again... again... Polonius, not even you can save your master from Hell this time.

I concede defeat on ever finding that book. The Hand of Dionysus, they call it. I find references, mentions, breadcrumbs. Did you know it's been mentioned as far back as Judas Iscariot, and even older still? Polonius, find the book so that no one must suffer, must die like this.

Time is nothing. Death is nothing. For the last hundred years alone I have lain in the garden, awaiting the trickle of my brother's poison in my ear a thousand times. Again and again and again. How cruel should it be that this gap of time seems to begin and end with me lying in the garden on a warm spring morning? How does my brother always find a way to kill me? Is his hatred of me truly so strong? And my wife—my wife, her faithfulness useless, meaningless, the bridal bed soiled with another's lust...

Let her have him if she loves him so much. Let them cavort in the halls of Elsinore, and some year hence, the chambers of Hell. I could not say goodbye to my only son. My regrets burn in my throat like acid, like poison. I can say goodbye only to you.

So farewell, my faithful advisor. Bury me far from Claudius if it's the last thing you do. I can hear the playmaster's foosteps in the hallway, here to relieve me from this endless madness. I give up. I give up.

要找到那本书，我认输了。他们称它为“狄俄尼索斯之手”。我找到了一些记载、提及它的文字、零星的线索。你知道吗，早在加略人犹大的时代，就有人提到过它，甚至还要更早？波洛涅斯，找到那本书，让所有人都不必再这样受苦、这样死去。

时间算不了什么。死亡算不了什么。仅仅过去这一百年，我就已在花园里躺过一千次，等着弟弟的毒药滴进我的耳朵。一次又一次，一次又一次。这段时间竟以我在温暖的春日清晨躺在花园里为起点，又以此为终点，这该是何等残酷？为什么弟弟总能找到杀我的办法？他对我的恨，当真如此深吗？还有我的妻子——我的妻子，她的忠贞毫无用处，毫无意义，新婚的床榻被另一个人的欲望玷污……

她既然那么爱他，就让她得到他吧。让他们在埃尔西诺的厅堂里尽情嬉闹，再过些年，就去地狱的房间里继续。我没能向我唯一的儿子道别。悔恨灼烧着我的喉咙，像酸液，像毒药。我只能向你道别。

那么，永别了，我忠诚的顾问。哪怕这是你最后能做的一件事，也要把我葬在远离克劳狄斯的地方。我听见了戏剧大师在走廊里的脚步声，他来让我摆脱这无尽的疯狂了。我放弃了。我放弃了。

source:
...And so it came to pass that the King of the Realm died one night, leaving his two sons behind. In this savage and warlike country, it was customary that whichever child inherited the crown for himself would immediately kill the others, eliminating further competition. However, these two brothers were twins, born within a scant few moments of one another. And so they brought the matter to High Executioner Selene.

They found her standing at the edge of the highest cliff in the kingdom, above the rolling and raging sea. 

"I am twenty seconds older than my brother," said the first prince. "Without any doubt at all, I am the rightful heir. Lady Selene, please cast my brother over this cliff immediately!" 

Lady Selene bound the second prince's hands and led him to the edge of the cliff. But the second prince sputtered, suddenly, "This is wrong! I may be younger, but my brother's body is weak and frail. He becomes sicker each day, and soon he may very well die. Then the Kingdom will be left with no heir at all! Don't kill me—kill him!"

Lady Selene paused to think a moment, then bound the first prince's hands, too.

The first prince spat with disgust. "My brother is a jealous imbecile!" Lady Selene wrapped a blindfold around his eyes.

The second prince stamped his foot. "My brother is a weakling and cannot see reason!" As with the first prince, the second prince, too, was soon blindfolded. Both of them continued to argue at the top of their lungs, screaming for the other one's demise.

Then the sound of Executioner Selene's fading footsteps caught their attention. "High Executioner, come back! You must kill my brother! I must be king! Where are you going?"

"I'm off to pour myself a flagon of wine and then pursue a career change to the next kingdom over, in that order," Selene replied. "Sounds like this one's gone a bit rotten. Good luck finding your way home with those blindfolds and binds on, lads."

The two men lunged at each other, unwilling to stand down. And the both of them went tipping over the edge, careening into the sea. The kingdom was none the worse for it, in the end.

source:
Your Highness,

Indeed as I am in your employ, it is my highest honor and duty to obey anything you might ask, including the neglect of your father's grave if you so wish. Still, might I ask why you desire this so strongly?

Alexander was a mighty ruler in his time. Whatever horrors he might have borne you and King Hamlet—may he rest in peace—are no more. In life we are cursed to continually remember the flaws of a man, but when viewed through the mirror of death, perhaps we might look upon such a man's flaws more kindly. The Lord smiles upon forgiveness for difficult men.

Nevertheless, I will continue to ensure his grave is not cleaned and no new gifts are laid there.

With all fidelity,

Alard the Groundskeeper

My glass shall not persuade me I am old
So long as youth and thou are one of date.
But when in thee time's furrows I behold,
Then look I death my days should expiate.
For all that beauty that doth cover thee
Is but the seemingly raiment of my heart
Which in thy breast doth live, as thine in mine.
How can I then be elder than thou art?
O therefore, love, be of thyself so wary
As I, not for myself, but for thee will,
Bearing thy heart, which I will keep so chary
As tender nurse her babe from faring ill.
Presume not on thy heart when mine is slain;
Thou gav'st me thine not to give back again.

source:
My Dearest Gertrude,

I hope this letter finds you in excellent health. Although I have not had the pleasure of your company in some years, I hope you will remember me fondly, Aunt, as I do you. I write to you with news of your sister, my most beloved Aunt Margaret.

Not one month ago, as one of her maids served a meal, the maid happened to drop a glass goblet, causing it to shatter. One of those shattered fragments entered Margaret's foot, and caused her to take gravely ill as the wound festered. Her physician recommended the limb be removed, and Margaret, then in good health, bade it be so. Yet on the very morning she was to undergo such a thing, she passed into the arms of God. You will be pleased to hear, I am certain, that the sacrament was administered in advance. May God rest her eternal soul.

I know that Margaret would have wanted you by her side in her final moments. Take comfort in the fact that she loved you dearly, and spoke of you often in her last few days.

Your faithful nephew,
Charles

source:
Have you often wondered at the true form and character of your lover? Pay careful mind: here are eight signs he's foe rather than friend! 

FIRST, within mere days of your acquaintance, he declares that if you 'call him but love, he'll be new baptis'd.' This nobleman is a walking source of dramatic show, clinging to any poor girl who crosses his path. Abnormally likely to meet his end in poison and tears.

SECOND, he uses the term 'taming' or 'shrew' in your presence—or even worse, in the same sentence. If he attempts to starve you to break your will, eat his heart out.

THIRD, he suddenly finds himself madly in love with your closest friend after promising you his undying heart. Keep a sharp eye out for faerie dust in the vicinity. 

FOURTH, he sticks a dagger in your back, then blames it on your 'ambition.' Don't worry: your restless spirit will have revenge. Stay indoors on March 15 if possible.

FIVE, after you help him murder his friends and cover up the crimes, he begins embarrassing you with inappropriate sobbing at your dinner parties. Even the most heartening prophecy can't revive this relationship. 

SIX, he tells you your wife has been unfaithful, but offers flimsy proof. Take a walk, enjoy some deep breathing, and stay away from pillows.

SEVEN, he tries to convince you to kill your brother. One might think this clear as day, yet this author is continually surprised.

EIGHT, sometimes he tells you to get to a nunnery. Other times he tells you he 'did love you once.' Which is it? Send this uncouth boy sulking back to university!

target: 教士管家

source: MARCH This morning I awoke from a vision of God as I slept. I saw Him before me in all His glory, and He spoke to me. When the dream faded, I realized my face was wet with tears. The Lord told me to enter the service of a certain Duke Iocus living in a town near here, and to oversee the man's baptism. This particular Duke was orphaned as a child, and as such, his holy education had been sorely neglected. I knew I had no choice but to obey God's will and to go seek out this man. That very dawn, I packed my things, paid the tab at my inn, and traveled over field and hill until I reached the gates of Duke Iocus's estate. Duke Iocus is a man of notorious reputation, to be certain; handsome, but wicked. Of course, as I have sworn a vow of modesty and chastity, I knew his wicked vices would have no influence on me. I knocked once and, hearing a shout, interpreted it as an invitation to enter. Imagine my surprise when I found the good Duke himself in the middle of beastly fornication with a young maiden... on the floor of the foyer, no less. The two of them were braying and sweating as nothing I'd ever seen. Flushing red, I coughed politely to make my presence known, but the Duke merely rolled over and lazily extended a hand in greeting. "Ahh, a cleric!" He boomed. "What brings you to my estate?" I introduced myself and declared my purpose to him, asking if he wished to be baptised. He roared with laughter. "What rubbish!" He explained to me that he had no need for a holy man, but all the need in the world for a stalwart butler... and so, before I could think of anything better, I agreed to serve him in that capacity. "I warn you, my new cleric butler," Iocus swore, "I shall never believe in any God you serve." He may say this now, but I believe I can change his heart. APRIL My lord Iocus has kept me busy this last month. One of my continual duties is to ensure the sanctity of his personal bedchamber, especially its cleanliness, so that he might continue to seduce all manner of impressionable young folk into it at all hours of the day and night. His lust seems to know no boundaries. I find it both frightening and some matter of clinical interest to me. Today, when tidying his chamber, I thought I might leave my bible at his bedside. Surely, I thought, he might read a page or two? I was right. He pushed into my room later that evening without knocking and handed the bible back to me. "What a fascinating book!" he declared. "Have you come to know God?" "Sort of. I read only the book called Song of Songs. I learned so many fascinating ways to compliment a woman's breasts. Never read anything so erotic in my life!" "And what of the rest of it, my liege?" He shrugged. "Dull. Dry. Lacking in action, heavy-handed on miracles to service the plot. Couldn't get through half of it without falling asleep." He spun on his heel and left. MAY For the last month, my lord Iocus kindly allowed me to bring a prayer group into his home. It is but once a week, on the sabbath. Tonight's subject was on preparing oneself to enter the communion of marriage and opening one's heart to God. Three young women and three young men came to our door, all of them in their finest clothing, ready to receive the Word. Ordinarily Iocus is prone to leaving home on nights like these to drink and play, but tonight he seemed compelled to linger. Not one hour in, after the wine had been served, Iocus came to me. "We've nothing to serve them to eat!" he fretted. "Nothing but bread and cheese. What sort of a meal is that? My good cleric, run into town and purchase an entire boar at once!" I donned my cloak, took a satchel of gold, and started off, giving the group my apologies. ...But three hours later, I returned to a scene which disturbed me to my core. Around the threshold of the front door were strewn half a dozen empty wineskins. Entering the foyer, I saw two of the young women giggling and chasing after the lads—all of them naked as babes and red in the face. From upstairs, I could faintly hear the sound of distant moans. "My Duke!" I called out. "What manner of sin is going on in this home?" Six voices rang out in muffled, sensual laughter. "What manner, indeed. I can be as specific as you like!" Duke Iocus called back, the seventh voice, barely stifling his own laugh. "Though we're, ah, preoccupied. Friends, make room in the bath—I'm coming in!" I think I must have gone into a dead faint, then. I knelt on the floor and prayed with all my might. Later that night, Iocus burst into my chambers. His hair was wild, his eyes rolling. He was stark naked. "Praise God!" He shouted. "I beg your pardon?" I said, bleary and half-awake. "My dear cleric, I've seen the light! I want you to baptise me immediately. Tomorrow at dawn, if possible!" "My lord," I said in shock, "What changed your mind?" Iocus shook his head. "I was nestled in a pile of limbs and lovemaking for hours. I thought for a moment I might die entwined like that. And I did experience a death, of sorts. But then, at the moment of release, a sense of utter peace came over me, the manner of which I can hardly describe. I've never felt so content! So magical! So right! I remembered all your endlessly dull lectures about the Holy Spirit. And I knew then that surely this must be your God's way of speaking through me. This must be how you feel every day!" I stared for a moment in horror. Neither of us spoke. "...So you'll be baptised?" I ventured after a long silence. "Right away, my good man. I want to be a Christian!" "Fair enough," I said, and went back to sleep. The Lord works in mysterious ways.
target: 三月 今晨，我从梦中上帝显现的异象里醒来。我看见祂在我面前，满身荣光，向我说话。梦境消散时，我才发现自己满脸泪水。主吩咐我去侍奉住在附近镇上的一位约库斯公爵，并负责为他施洗。这位公爵幼年便成了孤儿，因此，他的宗教教育被严重忽视了。我知道，我别无选择，唯有遵从上帝的旨意，去寻找此人。 就在那天黎明，我收拾好行李，结清旅店的账，穿过田野与山丘，直到来到约库斯公爵庄园的大门前。约库斯公爵确实声名狼藉；他相貌英俊，却品行邪恶。当然，我既已立下谦逊与贞洁的誓言，便知道他的邪恶恶习不会影响我。 我敲了一下门，听见一声喊叫，便当作是请我进去。想想我有多么吃惊吧：那位好公爵本人，竟正与一位年轻姑娘如野兽般交媾……而且就在门厅的地板上。两人嘶叫着，汗流浃背，那情形我从未见过。我满脸通红，礼貌地咳了一声，示意有人来了；公爵却只是翻了个身，懒洋洋地伸出一只手打招呼。“啊，一位教士！”他洪亮地说道，“什么风把你吹到我的庄园来了？” 我自报姓名，向他说明来意，问他是否愿意接受洗礼。他放声大笑。“一派胡言！”他向我解释，他不需要什么圣职人员，却急需一位尽职可靠的管家……于是，还没想到更好的办法，我就答应以管家的身份侍奉他。“我警告你，我的新教士管家，”约库斯郑重说道，“不管你侍奉什么上帝，我都绝不会信。” 他眼下或许这样说，但我相信，我能改变他的心意。 四月 过去这一个月，约库斯老爷让我忙得不可开交。我日常职责之一，就是确保他的私人寝室圣洁，尤其要保持干净，好让他日夜随时都能把各种容易受人影响的年轻人诱进房里。他的淫欲似乎毫无边界。我既觉得可怕，又从研究的角度对此有些兴趣。 今天收拾他的寝室时，我想，或许可以把我的《圣经》留在他床边。我心想，他总该会读上一两页吧？ 我猜对了。当天晚上，他没敲门便闯进我的房间，把《圣经》还给我。“真是本引人入胜的书！”他宣称。 “您已经认识上帝了吗？” “算是吧。我只读了那篇叫《雅歌》的。我学会了好多赞美女人胸脯的妙法。这辈子都没读过这么香艳的东西！” “那么其余的部分呢，老爷？” 他耸耸肩。“无聊。枯燥。没什么情节，倒是硬塞了不少奇迹来推动故事。还没读到一半就睡着了。”他转身便走。 五月 过去一个月，约库斯老爷好心允许我在他家中组织祈祷聚会。每周只有一次，就在安息日。今晚的主题是为步入婚姻的结合做好准备，并向上帝敞开心扉。三位年轻女子和三位年轻男子来到门前，个个都穿着自己最好的衣服，准备聆听圣言。通常这种晚上，约库斯总爱出门喝酒玩乐，可今晚他似乎忍不住要留下。 还不到一个小时，葡萄酒已经端上，约库斯便来找我。“我们没东西给他们吃！”他焦急地说，“只有面包和奶酪。这算哪门子饭？我的好教士，快进镇里去，立刻买一整头野猪回来！”我披上斗篷，带上一袋金币，向众人致歉后便出发了。 ……可三小时后，我回来所见的情景，却令我从心底感到不安。前门门槛四周，散落着六只空酒囊。走进门厅，我看见两位年轻女子咯咯笑着追逐那些小伙子——所有人都像初生婴儿一般赤裸，脸色通红。楼上传来隐约的呻吟声。 “公爵大人！”我喊道，“这屋里究竟在犯什么罪？”六个人发出低低的、充满情欲的笑声。 “究竟什么罪，这可问得好。你想听多详细，我都能说！”约库斯公爵回喊道，这是第七个人的声音，他自己也快憋不住笑了。“不过我们，啊，正忙着。朋友们，在浴池里腾个地方——我也来！” 我想，那时我一定已经昏厥过去了。我跪在地板上，用尽全力祈祷。 那天深夜，约库斯闯进我的寝室。他头发凌乱，眼珠乱转，全身赤裸。“赞美上帝！”他喊道。 “您说什么？”我睡眼惺忪，半梦半醒地问。 “亲爱的教士，我已看见了光！我要你立刻为我施洗。可以的话，就在明天黎明！” “老爷，”我惊愕地说，“是什么让您改变了心意？” 约库斯摇摇头。“我在交缠的肢体间温存了好几个小时。有那么一刻，我以为自己会就这样缠绕着死去。而我确实经历了一次死亡，某种意义上的。可就在释放的那一刻，一种无比安宁的感觉笼罩了我，我简直无法形容。我从没这么满足过！这么神奇！这么美好！我想起你那些关于圣灵的、没完没了的乏味说教。那时我便知道，这一定是你的上帝借我的身体传达旨意的方式。你每天一定都是这种感觉！” 我惊恐地瞪着他，一时无言。我们谁也没说话。沉默许久后，我试探着问：“……这么说，您愿意接受洗礼？” “立刻就来，我的好伙计。我要做个基督徒！” “那好吧。”我说完，便接着睡了。 主行事自有奥秘。

source: May Eve
target: 五月节前夜

source:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided -- just as Celeste's had been -- but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab -- a branch overhanging the pond -- and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'
target:
我记得塞莱斯特坐在最前面。

她领着五月节的游行队伍，身穿白色长裙，腰间系着蓝丝带，头发里编着鲜花。大家说，从没见过哪位五月女王有她一半漂亮。一辆辆相连的马车沿着镇上唯一的街道前行，她就坐在最前头，裙摆垂在腿下，双腿悬在车沿外。她光着脚，双脚白净，眼睛和腰间的丝带一样蓝。就连我也不得不承认，她很美。

我站在妈妈的小屋外，看着她经过。她转过头，对我微笑着喊道：“安娜！来跟我们一起跳舞吧！”她朝我伸出双手，系在手腕上的铃铛轻轻作响。毕竟，我们曾经是最好的朋友。

可走在她身旁的男孩们却嘲笑我。“丑八怪，小贱人！”其中一个尖声叫道。另一个扔来一块石头。“黄牙、呆脸、乱毛的废物！”还有一个拿着棍子朝我追来，像是要往我背上打，直到把棍子打断。

泪水盈满了我的眼睛，我退进树林。这里远离五月节游行的喧闹，一切都幽暗而寂静。树木像手指一样伸展在头顶，一时间，我在黑暗中忘了自己。我不知道自己去了哪里，只顾盯着长满苔藓的地面走。这里没有路。我也不需要路。

人真正迷路时，自己总是知道的。我就是如此。此时已近午夜，而我离开母亲家门时还是正午。一轮满月照着我前行，在林地上投下交错缠绕的影子。 

终于，我来到一片平静的湖边。我在那里向春天之灵祈祷，向那位伟大的女神祈祷——所有五月女王都是仿照她的形象装扮的。“让我像塞莱斯特一样美丽吧，”我哭喊道，“让我也配当五月女王吧！”

湖水分开了。一道波浪轻拍水面。接着，那匹母马缓缓从水底爬出来，一只蹄子接着一只蹄子。那是一匹白色的母马，浑身湿透，猛烈地甩着头，把水珠从鬃毛上甩落。这一定是女神亲自化作凡间的形体，显现在我面前。它的鬃毛也编成了辫子，和塞莱斯特的头发一样，只是编进去的是苔草，而不是鲜花。

母马站在我面前，金色的眼睛注视着我。终于，它开口了（它的嘴并不能动，却仍然发出了声音）：“人类的孩子，你是来向我求助的吗？”

“是的，”我轻声说，“我想变得美丽。像塞莱斯特一样美丽。”

它向我低下硕大的头，用鼻子蹭了蹭我的手。我轻柔地抚摸它，感受着它呼在我指上的气息。祈祷得到了回应，突如其来的宽慰涌上心头，我把脸埋进它的鬃毛里，抽泣起来。

“别哭，人类的孩子，”它对我说，“到我幽暗的水中来，重获新生，成为一位属于你自己的女神。只要爬上我的背，我们就一起下去。你终会成为五月女王。”

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

一个名字涌到嘴边，化作一声哽住的尖叫：“溪马！”

“是——啊——”水里的东西嘶声说道。它马一样的嘴唇向后掀起，露出尖利的牙齿。

我转身想游开，却感觉那些牙齿咬住了我的背。月亮在高高的水面上方越变越小，渐渐远得无法触及。四周柔和的绿色包围了我。我沉向水底的苔藓。不。那不是苔藓。是残骸。而我最后看见的，是那道尖牙毕露的狞笑。

“你永远成不了女王，”它嘶哑地说，“不过，你的骨头一定会很美。”

source: Walking The Low Beyond
target: 行于地下彼岸

source:
Hear me, young maidens who have traveled wild,
Whose eyes have never seen the touch of death,
Who tarry often when the sun grows dim,
Who linger long by cairns and caverns dark.

I once was you in spirit and in heart.
I am Persephone, the taken one.
When I was young I planted seeds alone,
And gathered flowers freely in the sun.

One day the earth burst forth with violent seams
And ashes belched with spite upon the land.
King Hades, Lord of Death, had come for me,
To seize and make me his unwilling bride.

At first I cried out to the world above,
But no one heard the call to grab my hand.
He pulled me down into the low beyond,
And I knew this was where I'd make my grave.

No flowers grew within the world of death.
I fell upon the ground and wept with fear.
As Hades offered me his outstretched hand,
I flinched from him and clenched my trembling fists.

He bade me then to take his hand's contents,
A small red fruit with tiny ruby seeds.
The god of many names, his countenance kind,
Pressed each small icy seed into my palm.

'Persephone, I'll never do you harm.
For years I've loved and watched you from afar.
Become my wife and you shall be the queen
Of everything that lives and moves about.

But if you wish to flee from me right now,
I'll trouble you no more and leave you be.
I brought you down here not to be your jailer,
But to show you the lands you might yet rule.'

Three days and nights I spent in Hades' world.
I grew to know his kingdom as my own.
When that third night fell on the river Styx,
I knew that I had made my final choice.

'I shall take these three seeds and be your bride,
If only you will grant me one small thing.
I wish to plant these seeds in darkness here,
And turn your endless winter into spring.'

So maidens, when you find you are now crones,
And when your kindest days all seem long past,
When winter sinks into your tired bones,
Prepare yourself to meet me then at last.

I'll guide you down the long unending halls
And bear you gently to the low beyond,
Where you will dine beside the ones you've lost
And join us in an everlasting bond.
target:
听我说，游历荒野的少女们，
你们的双眼尚未见过死亡，
常在日光渐暗时迟迟不归，
久久徘徊于石冢与幽暗洞穴旁。

我的心与灵魂也曾和你们一样。
我是珀耳塞福涅，被掳走的女子。
年轻时，我独自播下种子，
在阳光下自在地采集鲜花。

有一天，大地猛然裂开，
灰烬恶狠狠地喷涌，洒落大地。
冥王哈迪斯，死亡之主，为我而来，
要将我夺去，强娶为妻。

起初，我向地上的世界呼喊，
却无人听见，无人伸手拉住我。
他把我拉入地下的彼岸，
我知道，这里将是我的墓地。

死亡的世界里没有鲜花生长。
我倒在地上，恐惧地哭泣。
哈迪斯向我伸出手时，
我畏缩着躲开，攥紧颤抖的双拳。

随后，他让我接过掌中之物，
一颗红色的小果实，籽如细小的红宝石。
这位有着诸多名号的神，面容和善，
把一粒粒冰凉的种子放进我掌心。

“珀耳塞福涅，我绝不会伤害你。
多年来，我一直爱着你，从远处望着你。
做我的妻子，你便会成为女王，
统领一切活着、行走着的生灵。

但若你现在就想离我而去，
我便不再纠缠，任你离开。
我带你下来，并非要做你的狱卒，
而是让你看看将来或可统治的土地。”

我在哈迪斯的世界度过三天三夜。
渐渐熟悉他的王国，仿佛那是我的家园。
当第三个夜晚降临冥河斯堤克斯，
我知道，我已作出最后的选择。

“我愿收下这三粒种子，成为你的新娘，
只求你答应我一件小事。
我想把这些种子种在此处的黑暗里，
将你无尽的寒冬化作春天。”

所以，少女们，当你们也成了老妇，
当最美好的日子都仿佛远去，
当寒冬渗入你们疲惫的骨头，
就准备好，终于来与我相见吧。

我会引你们走过漫长无尽的厅堂，
轻柔地将你们带往地下彼岸，
在那里，你们将与逝去的亲人朋友同席，
与我们结下永恒的羁绊。

source: Alas, poor man. I knew him well.
target: 唉，可怜的人。我和他很熟。

source: Someone has carved a heart around the names on this one.

source: 'Kim and Dan McAuliffe: In death as in life, adventuring together.'
target: “金与丹·麦考利夫：生死如一，并肩冒险。”

source: It's nice to see not all love is fickle.
target: 看到爱情并非全都善变，真好。

source: 'Christopher L. Morrow: Urge no more words; I have no more to say.'
target: “克里斯托弗·L·莫罗：莫再催我开口；我已无话可说。”

source: There's poetry in that.
target: 这句话倒有些诗意。

target: “格蕾丝·凯利：唉，那件事本可以有个更好的结果。”

source: 'Bryant Woods: No great loss...'
target: “布莱恩特·伍兹：算不上什么大损失……”

source: Sir Woods must have been serenely humble, then. Or dreadfully boring.
target: 那伍兹爵士一定是个淡泊谦逊的人。或者，是个极其无趣的人。

target: “乔安妮·德拉吉奇：她以为能在雾中找到悬崖。可惜，她雾判了。”

target: “莎拉·维列加斯：帮我拿着蜜酒！”

source: 'Jesse Schell: PERICVLA VERITATI SAEPE CONTIGVA.'

source: The sweet are often the flowers that sooner drop their petals.
target: 美好的人往往如花，花瓣总是更早凋落。

source: Yorick's grave. He was the jester when I was young.

target: 这些是王室的墓。中间那座属于哈姆雷特的父亲，哈姆雷特国王。

source: Gertrude will soon be buried alongside him.

source: 'Lady Simona of Denmark.'
target: “丹麦的西蒙娜女士。”

source: The words on this tombstone have worn away with time...

source: It's locked.
target: 锁上了。

source: That door's locked.
target: 那扇门锁上了。

source: I ought not to leave just yet.
target: 我还不该离开。

source: The guards have locked up their chambers for the night.
target: 卫兵们已经把房间锁好过夜了。

source: Leartes locked the door. I guess he wants his privacy.
target: 雷欧提斯锁了门。我猜他不想被人打扰。

source: Hamlet's locked the door. I should... probably leave him be.
target: 哈姆雷特锁了门。我……大概还是别打扰他了。

source: The bar is closed. Othello has left by now.
target: 酒馆关门了。奥赛罗这会儿已经走了。

source: The castle cutlery. Irma keeps it spotless every night.
target: 城堡的餐具。伊尔玛每晚都会把它们擦得一尘不染。

source: All of Irma's various pots and pans.
target: 伊尔玛的各式锅具。

source: One of the guard's beds.
target: 一张卫兵的床。

source: It's... much less nice than mine.
target: 这……比我的床差多了。

source: Hmm. 'A Treatise on Divine-Given Morality.'
target: 嗯。《论神赐的道德》。

source: I had no idea our guard staff were so well read.
target: 我还不知道我们的卫兵如此博览群书。

source: What is that woman doing?
target: 那个女人在做什么？

source: I take back what I said before.
target: 我收回刚才的话。

source: When some new man joins the unit, they'll put their personal items here.
target: 有新人加入卫队时，就会把私人物品放在这里。

source: Playing cards, and winnings.
target: 纸牌，还有赢来的钱。

source: I'm surprised Marcellus just leaves this all out in the open.
target: 马塞勒斯竟然就把这些全摆在外面。

source: Horatio's personal effects are here, what little of them he has.
target: 霍拉旭的私人物品在这里，本来也没几件。

source: He's not strictly a guard, but the King gave him quarters on Hamlet's request.

source: What's this?

source: But I can't stop reading.

source: Hard to believe Father has something like this in his room.

source: Ah. I borrowed this from the gallery some time ago.

source: It's certainly not a very uplifting tale.

source: It's a book of poetry.

source: Persephone... A girl taken from her homeland and made a Queen.

source: Hamlet's gone and blocked out all the light. How juvenile.
target: 哈姆雷特把光全遮住了。真幼稚。

source: If I want to sleep a while, it should be in my own room.
target: 要是想睡一会儿，我该回自己的房间。

source: If I want to take a nap, it should be in my own room.
target: 要是想打个盹，我该回自己的房间。

source: This is where the Queen has her hair done. A mirror of this size must have taken a long while to build.
target: 王后就在这里让人梳理头发。这么大的镜子，做起来一定花了很长时间。

source: Oh, Laertes... What could you possibly need all these blades for?
target: 唉，雷欧提斯……你到底要这么多刀剑做什么？

source: Elsinore castle looks enormous, even this far away.
target: 即使离得这么远，埃尔西诺城堡看起来依然十分庞大。

source: It may look shallow, but it's deceptively deep.
target: 看着可能很浅，其实深得很。

source: I used to play here as a girl. Now, though, with all these heavy skirts... better steer clear.
target: 我小时候常在这里玩。不过现在，穿着这么沉的裙子……还是离远点好。

source: These were carved, I'm told, after the last time Elsinore was sieged and rebuilt.
target: 听说这些雕像是在埃尔西诺上一次遭到围攻、重建之后雕成的。

source: It's the Danish coat of arms.
target: 这是丹麦的纹章。

source: It's late, I should really go to bed.
target: 很晚了，我真该去睡了。

source: I have no reason to head to the docks right now.
target: 我现在没理由去码头。

source: That way lies eastward, out into the Sound.
target: 那边通往东面，出去就是厄勒海峡。

source: Denmark controls the waterway here. All passing ships must stop and pay their tolls to us.
target: 丹麦控制着这里的航道。所有过往船只都必须停下来，向我们缴纳通行税。

source: The Royal Fleet of Denmark is anchored close by. This harbor is rather shallow, so longboats come ashore to ferry passengers to and fro.
target: 丹麦皇家舰队就停泊在附近。这个港口水很浅，所以要用长艇往返岸边接送乘客。

source: It's a note bearing the Seal of the King.
target: 这是一封盖着国王印玺的信。

source: Hamlet's looking at it right now. I can't get close.
target: 哈姆雷特现在正在看。我没法靠近。

source: 'I've entrusted these orders to two loyal servants, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, to ensure that...'
target: “我已将这些命令交托给罗森克兰兹和吉尔登斯吞这两位忠诚的仆人，以确保……”

source: '...To be executed upon arrival.'
target: “……抵达后即刻处决。”

source: This is a death warrant for Hamlet, written by Claudius. It'll never reach England now.
target: 这是克劳狄斯写下的、处死哈姆雷特的命令。现在它再也不会送到英格兰了。

source: Still, I wonder if... Rosencrantz and Guildenstern were carrying this letter intentionally.
target: 不过，我还是想知道……罗森克兰兹和吉尔登斯吞是不是有意带着这封信。

source: My assumption is deception on all sides.
target: 我猜各方都在骗人。

source: That way leads to the stables. Nothing in there but a lot of muck and mares.
target: 那边通往马厩。里面除了成堆的粪便和母马，什么都没有。

source: That way leads into the fields. I can see the hills roll for miles. Regardless, I've no interest in leaving town.
target: 那边通往田野。我能看见起伏的丘陵绵延数英里。不过，我没兴趣离开镇子。

source: If I knew how to steer a ship, I could go anywhere.
target: 要是我会掌舵，就能去任何地方。

source: But as is, I would probably only wind up at the bottom of the ocean.
target: 可就凭我现在的本事，大概只会落得沉到海底的下场。

source: There's so little light in here.
target: 这里光线真暗。

source: This is where prisoners sleep. Or... try to sleep, I'd guess.
target: 囚犯就在这里睡觉。或者……我猜，只能说试着睡着吧。

source: Lord have mercy. Lord have mercy.
target: 主啊，求你怜悯。主啊，求你怜悯。

source: Please, god, please god, please.
target: 求求你，上帝，求求你，上帝，求求你。

source: Lord have mercy, please god, have mercy.
target: 主啊，求你怜悯，上帝，求求你，发发慈悲。

source: Don't let her kill me. Please. Protect us.
target: 别让她杀了我。求求你。保佑我们。

source: Father has likely already gone to bed.
target: 父亲大概已经上床睡觉了。

source: Father always fancied himself a scholar, I think. He certainly carried on like one.
target: 我想，父亲从前总以学者自居。他的言谈举止确实也像个学者。

source: Father fancies himself a scholar, I think. He certainly carries on like one.
target: 我想，父亲以学者自居。他的言谈举止确实也像个学者。

source: These must be Bernardo's things. That was his father's dagger. He died two summers ago.
target: 这些一定是贝尔纳多的东西。那把匕首原本是他父亲的。他父亲在两年前的夏天去世了。

source: It's... my mother's grave. Elise.
target: 这是……我母亲的坟墓。伊莉丝。

source: She died before I can even remember. I know Father loved her a lot.
target: 我还没记事，她就去世了。我知道父亲很爱她。

source: This massive fireplace is kept burning by the servants day and night. It's the true castle hearth, I suppose.
target: 仆人们让这座巨大的壁炉日夜燃烧。我想，它才是城堡真正的炉火中心。

source: The cell door is locked right now.
target: 牢门现在锁着。

source: Could I have actually broken free?
target: 难道我真的已经挣脱了？

source: Please, God, let it be so.
target: 上帝啊，求你让这一切是真的。

source: Irma maintains these plants herself. I guess it's her hobby.
target: 这些植物都是伊尔玛亲自照料的。我猜这是她的爱好。

source: TODO THIS IS A FASCINATING YET INDESCRIBABLE OBJECT
target: 待完成：这是个令人着迷却又难以描述的东西

source: Father's hearth. It looks warm.
target: 父亲的壁炉。看起来很暖和。

source: Just books, here.
target: 这里只有书。

source: The servants draw water from this well to wash our belongings.
target: 仆人们从这口井里打水，清洗我们的物品。

source: It's uncomfortably warm in here, considering the season. But I suppose Hamlet likes it this way.
target: 这个季节，屋里这么热实在让人不舒服。不过我想哈姆雷特就喜欢这样。

source: Astrid...
target: 阿斯特丽德……

source: Various herbs, ingredients, and salted meat. All of Irma's raw materials.
target: 各种香草、食材和腌肉。都是伊尔玛做饭用的原料。

source: Irma's hearth, used to cook and bake every meal.
target: 伊尔玛的炉灶，每顿饭都在这里烹煮烘烤。

source: It rarely seems to sputter out entirely--Irma is always working.
target: 它似乎很少会彻底熄灭——伊尔玛总在忙活。

source: It rarely seems to sputter out entirely—Irma is always working.
target: 它似乎很少会彻底熄灭——伊尔玛总在忙活。

source: My dresser, where some of my simpler garments are kept.
target: 我的衣柜，里面放着一些比较朴素的衣服。

source: I'm partial to this gown, though.
target: 不过，我还是偏爱这条裙子。

source: There are armed guards outside. I don't think they'll take kindly to my trying to leave.
target: 外面有武装卫兵。我想，要是我试着离开，他们不会高兴的。

source: No sense in going all the way down there right now.
target: 现在没必要一路走下去到那儿。

source: The castle armory is well stocked.
target: 城堡的军械库储备充足。

source: I can't sleep now.
target: 我现在不能睡。

source: Father's desk, as messy as ever.
target: 父亲的书桌，还是一如既往地乱。

source: The gate is locked.
target: 大门锁着。

source: It's unlocked.
target: 没锁。

source: And... empty.
target: 而且……是空的。

source: Nothing's hidden here.
target: 这里没藏什么东西。

source: The gate to town is locked.
target: 通往镇上的大门锁着。

source: I still won't touch that bucket.
target: 我还是不愿碰那个桶。

source: This bar's fireplace has a pleasant feel to it.
target: 这间酒馆的壁炉让人觉得很舒服。

source: Better rest my head a while.
target: 最好躺下休息一会儿。

source: I'm not tired right now.
target: 我现在不累。

source: Wha... what time is it?
target: 什……现在几点了？

source: I suppose I was more exhausted from the previous night than I'd thought...
target: 看来昨晚让我比想象中还要疲惫……

source: It's far too late for me to have remained in bed.
target: 我竟然睡到现在，实在太晚了。

source: No point. I know what's down there.
target: 没必要。我知道下面有什么。

source: Not that it does us any good when Fortinbras arrives.
target: 可等福丁布拉斯来了，这些也帮不了我们。

source: No need to look through his things anymore if he's not here.
target: 如果他不在这里，就没必要再翻他的东西了。

source: What are you doing amongst my personal effects?
target: 你在我的私人物品里翻什么？

source: Leave me and my items be.
target: 别烦我，也别碰我的东西。

source: (I suppose I ought to wait until he's gone to rummage around...)
target: （看来我该等他走了再翻找……）

source: There are some notes inside the chest.
target: 箱子里有一些笔记。

source: Something's very wrong. He's so cryptic... what does he mean? What did he see?
target: 很不对劲。他写得这么隐晦……到底是什么意思？他看到了什么？

source: I refuse to believe Hamlet's in this state on my behalf alone.
target: 我不相信哈姆雷特变成这样，仅仅是因为我。

source: I need to have a closer look at the gallery.
target: 我得去画廊仔细看看。

source: A-and, combined with the report I found in the gallery...
target: 再、再加上我在画廊找到的那份报告……

source: Can this be saying... King Hamlet's death... that he was... killed?
target: 这难道是在说……哈姆雷特国王的死……他是……被人杀害的？

source: No. I have no proof of that. I should keep a close eye on Hamlet.
target: 不。我没有证据。我得密切留意哈姆雷特。

source: He'll lead me to the truth. I'm sure of it.
target: 他会带我找到真相的。我确信。

source: So Hamlet suspected his father was murdered even before he knew.
target: 原来哈姆雷特还没得知真相，就已经怀疑父亲是被谋杀的了。

source: So Hamlet suspects his father was murdered after all.
target: 原来哈姆雷特果然怀疑父亲是被谋杀的。

source: This old shack is older than I am, but not by much.
target: 这间旧棚屋比我年纪还大，不过也没大多少。

source: This is where all of the plague victim's things were stored. Including my mother's.
target: 瘟疫死者的东西全都存放在这里。也包括我母亲的。

source: I can see nails coming through from the other side. It won't budge for my weight.
target: 我能看见从另一面钉穿过来的钉子。凭我的体重，撞不动它。

source: I need someone stronger. Who might want to help?
target: 我需要一个力气更大的人。谁会愿意帮忙呢？

source: This is the lazzaretto where my mother was held...
target: 这就是母亲当年被隔离的疫病所……

source: I'm not certain what that dock-shack is for. It's been locked up tight for as long as I can remember.
target: 我不太清楚码头那间棚屋是做什么用的。从我记事起，它就一直锁得严严实实。

source: When the Book erased them, where did they go, I wonder?
target: 那本书抹去他们的时候，他们去了哪里呢？

source: Am I damned? Is this hell?
target: 我受到了永罚吗？这里是地狱吗？

source: What kind of God could allow this to happen?
target: 什么样的上帝会容许这种事发生？

source: I hope you're at peace, father.
target: 父亲，希望您已经安息。

source: I've come here to pray before the Virgin ever since I was a girl. When I think of praying these days... nothing comes to mind.
target: 从小我就来这里，在圣母面前祈祷。可最近想到祈祷时……我却什么也想不出来。

source: The King's bedchamber is under even tighter watch than Gertrude's.
target: 国王寝室的守卫比乔特鲁德那边还严。

source: Even now, I'll have to wait for Claudius to invite me in again.
target: 即使现在，我也得等克劳狄斯再次邀请我进去。

source: I've been in there before. But only when... well...
target: 我以前进去过。但只有在……嗯……

source: Only in worlds where the Queen's passed away.
target: 只有在王后已经去世的那些世界里。

source: I've been in there before, when Claudius held private council over Fortinbras's hiding out nearby.
target: 我以前进去过，当时克劳狄斯召集秘密议事，商讨福丁布拉斯藏身附近的事。

source: But... I wonder if it's possible to find a way to explore that room on my own.
target: 不过……不知道能不能想个办法，独自探查那间房间。

source: Only two people have ever been allowed inside, as far as I know: the Queen, when the two of them are 'together'...
target: 据我所知，只有两个人获准进去过：王后，在他们俩“共处”的时候……

source: And Bernardo, who comes to deliver private news to him from time to time.
target: 还有贝尔纳多，他偶尔会来向国王私下汇报消息。

source: Not even my father is permitted entry unless the circumstances are dire.
target: 除非情况危急，否则连我父亲也不许进去。

source: Hmm. Father locked his door. That's unlike him.
target: 嗯。父亲把房门锁了。这可不像他。

source: There are a lot of books here, but I see the bit of parchment I'm looking for.
target: 这里有很多书，不过我看见要找的那张羊皮纸了。

source: 'Uncommon circumstances?'
target: “情况异常？”

source: I wonder how much Hamlet suspects of his father's death.
target: 不知道哈姆雷特对父亲的死有多少怀疑。

source: ... And to what extent a snake was really involved.
target: ……还有，那条蛇究竟在其中起了多大作用。

source: I cannot act without evidence. I must follow Hamlet, and see where his path leads him. ...For now.
target: 没有证据，我不能行动。我得跟着哈姆雷特，看看他会走向何处。……暂且如此。

source: It's clear that Claudius took great pains to cover up his crime. Such a sad, unfortunate man.
target: 显然，克劳狄斯为了掩盖罪行煞费苦心。他真是个可悲又不幸的人。

source: This shelf is cluttered with books, both old and new.
target: 这架子上乱堆着各种新旧书籍。

source: This is a perfect source of linen. Horatio can use this to make canvas.
target: 这里正好有亚麻布。霍拉旭可以用它做画布。

source: Er... I'll use one of my older garments.
target: 呃……就用我一件旧衣服吧。

source: I now have everything Horatio needed. Just need to find a time with he and Brit are both free.
target: 霍拉旭需要的东西，现在都齐了。只要找个他和布莉特都有空的时间。

source: Gertrude mentioned she'd hid Brit's letters somewhere with 'unheard wishes'. A wishing well does make sense.
target: 乔特鲁德提过，她把布莉特的信藏在了一个有“无人听见的愿望”的地方。许愿井确实说得通。

source: Let me see... ah!
target: 让我看看……啊！

source: There's a loose stone inside the well. And... here they are.
target: 井里有块松动的石头。而且……信就在这里。

source: I'll bring these to Brit as soon as she's free.
target: 布莉特一有空，我就把这些交给她。

source: Ah! There are some eggs here.
target: 啊！这里有些鸡蛋。

source: Don't even think about 'borrowing' from my food stores.
target: 别想从我的食物储备里“借”东西。

source: I promise you, you won't like the consequences.
target: 我保证，后果有你好受的。

source: (...Maybe later...)
target: （……还是晚点再说吧……）

source: Better collect them to give to Horatio.
target: 还是把它们拿上，交给霍拉旭吧。

source: This is a perfect source of charcoal. Better collect some to give Horatio.
target: 这里正好有木炭。还是拿一些给霍拉旭吧。

source: How did my father find anything on a desk this messy?
target: 桌子这么乱，父亲以前怎么找得到东西？

source: Father, how do you find anything on a desk this messy?
target: 父亲，桌子这么乱，您怎么找得到东西？

source: Messy? What on earth do you mean? It's organized precisely the way I like it!
target: 乱？你这话到底是什么意思？我就是喜欢这样摆的！

source: It's unclear how Father finds anything on a desk this messy.
target: 真不知道父亲怎么在这么乱的桌子上找到东西。

source: Hmm—there's a note here.
target: 嗯——这里有张便条。

source: A missing lute... I wonder if I could find it for him?
target: 一把丢失的鲁特琴……不知道我能不能帮他找到？

source: That's the late Queen Astrid, Hamlet's grandmother.
target: 那是已故的阿斯特丽德王后，哈姆雷特的祖母。

source: Come to think of it, I've often heard about King Alexander, but nothing about Queen Astrid. I wonder why?
target: 说起来，我常听人提起亚历山大国王，却从没听过阿斯特丽德王后的事。这是为什么呢？

source: How peculiar.
target: 真奇怪。

source: She looks so peaceful there.
target: 画里的她看起来那么安详。

source: Hard to imagine her dying the way she did.
target: 很难想象她竟会那样死去。

source: What are you rummaging around over there for? You know those books are the oldest in the gallery, right? They're delicate.
target: 你在那边翻来翻去找什么？你知道那些是画廊里最古老的书吧？它们很容易损坏。

source: Oh. I was only... looking for something new to read.
target: 哦。我只是……想找点没读过的书。

source: See?
target: 看到了吧？

source: That's a book on pregnancy sickness.
target: 那是一本讲孕吐的书。

source: Something you want to tell me?
target: 你有什么事想告诉我吗？

source: Ah. No.
target: 啊。没有。

source: (I just grabbed the first book I saw...)
target: （我只是随手拿了第一本看到的书……）

source: You're so strange.
target: 你真奇怪。

source: It's an old bookshelf—but tucked away between these books, there's a bound set of notes...
target: 这是个旧书架——不过这些书之间，藏着一册装订好的笔记……

source: ...The notes bear the emblem of a noble Danish house. ...House Brockenhuus. Brit's family?
target: ……笔记上印着一个丹麦贵族家族的纹章。……布罗肯胡斯家族。布莉特的家族？

source: Why would Brit keep personal notes in the gallery...?
target: 布莉特为什么要把私人笔记放在画廊里……？

source: '... No longer shall we meet before three in the morning. The docks are too busy at any other hour.' The docks... Hmm.
target: “……今后我们不再于凌晨三点之前见面。其他时间码头都太繁忙。”码头……嗯。

source: It sounds like she's meeting someone late at night. But who? And why?
target: 看来她在深夜与某个人见面。可那是谁？又是为什么？

source: These are the letters from Fortinbras's emissary. Brit evidently hid them here.
target: 这些是福丁布拉斯的使者寄来的信。显然是布莉特把它们藏在这里的。

source: This is where Brit hid her notes.
target: 布莉特就是把笔记藏在这里的。

source: Another old, dusty bookshelf.
target: 又一个积满灰尘的旧书架。

source: I could never have been the savior you wanted. Not really.
target: 我从来都不可能成为你想要的救世主。真正意义上的救世主。

source: It's Hamlet's father, and his namesake, the late King Hamlet.
target: 这是哈姆雷特的父亲，已故的哈姆雷特国王。哈姆雷特的名字也是沿用他的。

source: ...Come to think of it, I noticed a blank space on the walls in the gallery...
target: ……说起来，我注意到画廊墙上有一处空白……

source: ...Sorry that I doubted you. I promise we'll stop Quince.
target: ……对不起，我曾怀疑过你。我保证，我们会阻止昆斯。

source: ...I liked him enough when he was alive, now that he's dead I'm not sure what to make of him.
target: ……他活着的时候，我对他印象还不错。如今他死了，我反倒不知道该怎么看他了。

source: ...Could the King's ghost really be haunting this castle?
target: ……国王的幽灵真的在这座城堡里游荡吗？

source: I recognize her handwriting. This must be it.
target: 我认得她的笔迹。一定就是这个。

source: Mother's diary...
target: 母亲的日记……

source: Simona. She was trapped in time just like me.
target: 西蒙娜。她曾经和我一样，被困在时间里。

source: She's been through this before. She must know the way out of it all. And-- and if this is right, she's still alive!
target: 她以前经历过这些。她一定知道怎么摆脱这一切。而且——而且如果这是真的，她还活着！

source: She's been through this before. She must know the way out of it all. And—and if this is right, she's still alive!
target: 她以前经历过这些。她一定知道怎么摆脱这一切。而且——而且如果这是真的，她还活着！

source: But where is she?
target: 可她在哪里？

source: This is... incredible. If this is true... I've got to find Simona and speak to her.
target: 这真是……难以置信。如果这是真的……我得找到西蒙娜，和她谈谈。

source: Sounds like she's living in town nearby.
target: 看来她住在附近的镇上。

source: Still hard to believe, even now.
target: 即使到了现在，还是难以相信。

source: I still need to see if I can find Simona. She must know something more.
target: 我还是得看看能不能找到西蒙娜。她一定还知道些什么。

source: To think that Simona escaped Quince for so many years.
target: 真没想到，西蒙娜竟然躲过了昆斯这么多年。

source: I wonder what she must have gone through, living all alone, unable to share what she'd been through with anyone.
target: 她独自生活，无法向任何人诉说自己的经历，不知道她究竟承受了些什么。

source: It's my father's lockbox. He kept all his personal items in there.
target: 这是父亲的上锁箱子。他以前把所有私人物品都放在里面。

source: It's my father's lockbox. He keeps his personal items in there.
target: 这是父亲的上锁箱子。他把私人物品放在里面。

source: Nothing but the key can open it, I presume.
target: 我想，只有钥匙才能打开它。

source: ...But it's unlockable now.
target: ……不过现在可以开锁了。

source: There are pages in here, scattered and frayed.
target: 里面散落着一些纸页，边缘都磨破了。

source: H-how could... this reads like... it's almost as if...
target: 怎、怎么会……这些文字读起来……简直就像……

source: As if time were repeating for him, too.
target: 就像他的时间也在不断重复。

source: Is this what Father was afraid I'd find? The mad rantings of a man in my exact predicament?
target: 这就是父亲怕我找到的东西吗？一个与我处境完全相同的人留下的疯言疯语？

source: He mentions a strange cursed book—what he was searching for, his way out—perhaps if I can find it... there's still an escape.
target: 他提到一本奇怪的受诅咒的书——他一直在寻找的东西，他的出路——也许只要我能找到它……就还有逃脱的希望。

source: No wonder Father didn't want the others to find out about this.
target: 难怪父亲不想让别人发现这些。

source: Everyone saw Hamlet as a strong king. No one ever thought him insane.
target: 所有人都认为哈姆雷特是位强大的国王。从没人觉得他疯了。

source: But if people believe that insanity runs in the family's bloodline...
target: 可如果人们相信，疯病会在这个家族里遗传……

source: Then that's cause to remove not just Hamlet, but Gertrude and Claudius from Elsinore.
target: 那就有理由把哈姆雷特、乔特鲁德和克劳狄斯都赶出埃尔西诺了。

source: It's empty. Nothing but... ashes.
target: 空了。只剩下……灰烬。

source: I've often heard him open and close it in the evenings. I know he had something in here, but... I'm too late.
target: 我常在晚上听见他打开又关上这个箱子。我知道他在里面放了东西，可……我来晚了。

source: A-ha! And here is Irma's key to Gertrude's Chambers.
target: 啊哈！伊尔玛那把乔特鲁德寝室的钥匙就在这里。

source: I already retrieved the key Irma hid here.
target: 伊尔玛藏在这里的钥匙，我已经拿走了。

source: The Queen has a private hearth to toast her feet at night, of course. It vents through the center of the castle tower.
target: 王后当然有自己的壁炉，晚上用来烤脚取暖。烟道从城堡塔楼的中央穿过。

source: This massive fireplace... it's kept burning by the servants day and night. It's the true castle hearth, I suppose.
target: 这座巨大的壁炉……仆人们让它日夜燃烧。我想，这才是城堡真正的炉火吧。

source: Hmmm. Locked.
target: 嗯……锁着。

source: What're yeh doin' here, my lady?
target: 小姐，您在这儿干什么呢？

source: I dunnah how you got yerself a key, but the Queen's chambers are private!
target: 我不知道您怎么弄到的钥匙，可王后的寝室不能随便进！

source: (Evidently I must attempt this when he's gone.)
target: （看来我得等他走了再试。）

source: And now it isn't. Key, meet keyhole.
target: 现在就不锁着了。钥匙，来认识一下锁孔。

source: The key to this room is supposed to be hidden in the planter...
target: 这间房的钥匙应该藏在花盆里……

source: Who would have access to Gertrude's chambers?
target: 谁能进出乔特鲁德的寝室呢？

source: I know Father will be... killed here.
target: 我知道父亲会在这里……被杀。

source: If I can get inside somehow... I can be there when it happens.
target: 如果我能想办法进去……那件事发生时，我就能在场了。

source: Father has been killed here before.
target: 父亲以前曾在这里被杀。

source: Father was murdered here.
target: 父亲是在这里被谋杀的。

source: I wonder if it's possible to find a way to enter Queen Gertrude's room and understand what happened.
target: 不知道能不能找到办法，进入乔特鲁德王后的房间，弄清楚发生了什么。

source: I suppose the Queen must want her privacy.
target: 我想，王后一定不希望有人打扰吧。

source: Forgive me, Lady Ophelia, but I cannot let you leave.
target: 请原谅，奥菲莉娅小姐，但我不能让您离开。

source: The King himself ordered that I disbar you.
target: 是国王亲自下令，让我禁止您外出的。

source: And now His Majesty is dead.
target: 可如今陛下已经死了。

source: T-the way you said that... Your face...!
target: 您、您说这话的语气……您的表情……！

source: Go right ahead, Lady Ophelia. My apologies.
target: 您请便，奥菲莉娅小姐。抱歉。

source: I still know about your little gambling ring, Cygnus.
target: 西格纳斯，我可还知道你们那个小赌局的事。

source: With all due respect, that ain't enough to overrule a member of the Royal Family's word.
target: 恕我直言，光凭这个还不足以让我违抗王室成员的命令。

source: (...This won't work. I need to find someone who has the power to help me regain access.)
target: （……这样不行。我得找个有权力的人，帮我恢复通行许可。）

source: Ah! I see. Perhaps I ought to tell the Guard Captain about your gambling ring, then?
target: 啊！我明白了。那我是不是该把你们赌局的事告诉卫队长呢？

source: What? Y-you... know about that?
target: 什么？您、您……知道这事？

source: Er... I'll let you through. Just please don't tell Bernardo about what you saw. He'll have all of us running laps for hours.
target: 呃……我让您过去。只是求您别把看到的事告诉贝尔纳多。他会罚我们所有人跑上好几个小时的。

source: Especially not after yeh ratted us out to Bernardo. My thighs are still pudding. I can hardly stand!
target: 您向贝尔纳多告了我们一状以后，就更不行了。我的大腿还软得像布丁，连站都快站不住！

source: Dunnah how you found out about our gambling, but... y'must be some kind of sorceress...
target: 不知道您怎么发现我们赌博的，不过……您一定是个会法术的女巫……

source: If I can learn about that, what other dirty secrets might I find if I spend long enough in the guard chambers?
target: 既然我能发现这件事，那要是我在卫兵的房间里多待一阵，又会发现别的什么见不得人的秘密呢？

source: ...As I was sayin', go right on ahead, m'lady. The gates are open.
target: ……就像我刚才说的，您请便，小姐。大门开着呢。

source: Ah. Yeh saw us, then. Hell. I knew our secret'd get out eventually...
target: 啊。原来您看见我们了。该死。我就知道这秘密迟早会泄露……

source: Er, I'll let you through. Just please don't tell Bernardo about what you saw. He'll have all of us running laps for hours.
target: 呃，我让您过去。只是求您别把看到的事告诉贝尔纳多。他会罚我们所有人跑上好几个小时的。

source: Why not? I'd like to go for a stroll.
target: 为什么不行？我想出去散散步。

source: Your father decreed to Guard Captain Bernardo that you were not to leave the castle grounds after... well... you and Hamlet.
target: 您的父亲吩咐过卫队长贝尔纳多，不许您离开城堡范围，是在……嗯……您和哈姆雷特那件事之后。

source: And with all of us guards on thin ice lately, I'd hate to anger the Guard Captain.
target: 而且最近我们这些卫兵都得小心行事，我可不想惹卫队长生气。

source: At least, not before I recoup my losses tomorrow night!—Er, I've said too much.
target: 至少也得等我明晚把输的钱赢回来！——呃，我说得太多了。

source: (Hmm. Sounds like there's more to this situation.)
target: （嗯。看来这事另有隐情。）

source: (I wonder if the other guards know more.)
target: （不知道其他卫兵是不是知道得更多。）

source: Ugh.
target: 呃。

source: (Maybe if I knew what they were getting up to in the evenings.)
target: （要是我知道他们晚上都在干些什么，也许就有办法了。）

source: The gate's locked. Cygnus must have stepped out. Hopefully he'll return shortly.
target: 大门锁着。西格纳斯一定是暂时离开了。希望他很快就回来。

source: It's Gertrude's diary.
target: 这是乔特鲁德的日记。

source: Ophelia, what are you doing?
target: 奥菲莉娅，你在做什么？

source: That's private.
target: 那是私人物品。

source: (Right. Can't have a look while she's here.)
target: （好吧。她在这里，我就没法看。）

source: I'm right here. Hoping to open her little diary?
target: 我就在这里呢。你想翻开她的小日记？

source: Oh, don't worry, I've already read the whole thing, obviously. But you don't have that privilege.
target: 哦，别担心，我当然早就从头到尾看过了。不过你可没有这个特权。

source: Get out before I report you.
target: 赶紧出去，不然我就告发你。

source: Oh, no. Gertrude...
target: 哦，不。乔特鲁德……

source: This is the information Hamlet wanted. Let's see what he wants to do with it.
target: 这就是哈姆雷特想要的信息。看看他打算怎么用吧。

source: This... this information could really tear apart the court.
target: 这……这些信息真的可能让宫廷分崩离析。

source: It's a letter. Hmm.
target: 是一封信。嗯。

source: Is something troubling you?
target: 有什么事让你烦心吗？

source: What are these papers?
target: 这些文件是什么？

source: Nothing of consequence. Come away from them.
target: 没什么要紧的。别在那边待着了。

source: (Right. Can't have a look while he's here.)
target: （好吧。他在这里，我就没法看。）

source: T-this is...
target: 这、这是……

source: Claudius must have hated his father far more than I realized.
target: 克劳狄斯对父亲的恨，一定比我原先以为的深得多。

source: Ophelia?
target: 奥菲莉娅？

source: Apologies, my lord. I was, er, trying to leave without waking you.
target: 抱歉，陛下。我是，呃，想悄悄离开，免得吵醒您。

source: I see.
target: 我明白了。

source: If you'd like to return to your chambers, you're free to go, of course.
target: 如果你想回自己的房间，当然随时可以走。

source: I wonder if there's something inside this vase...
target: 不知道这只花瓶里是不是藏着什么……

source: This vase has fingerprints on it. Is there something inside?
target: 这个花瓶上有指纹。里面有东西吗？

source: It needs dusting. I'll have to have my wife arrange for the servants to come by.
target: 该掸掸灰了。我得让妻子安排仆人过来清理。

source: There's something in here.
target: 这里面有东西。

source: (A... vial?)
target: （一只……小瓶？）

source: (It stinks of... some kind of noxious fumes.)
target: （它散发着……某种有毒气体的臭味。）

source: (This must be the poison he used to kill King Hamlet.)
target: （这一定是他用来杀害哈姆雷特国王的毒药。）

source: (I'd better pocket it.)
target: （我最好把它装进口袋。）

source: {It's... empty.}
target: {里面……空了。}

source: {But there is a lingering smell. Something was hidden here.)
target: {但还有气味残留。这里曾经藏着什么东西。)

source: Is this a drawer inlaid into the table?
target: 这是嵌在桌子里的抽屉吗？

source: What's inside this drawer, my lord?
target: 陛下，这个抽屉里是什么？

source: It hasn't been opened in years. I'm certain the hinges are rusted shut.
target: 它已经好几年没打开过了。我敢肯定，铰链都锈死了。

source: Someone left a bucket here. It looks like it's full of something.
target: 有人在这里放了个桶。看起来里面装满了什么东西。

source: Oh. Eurgh.
target: 哦。呕。

source: Well, I certainly regret looking in there. If this is meant to be a chamberpot, no one's cleaned it in ages.
target: 好吧，我真后悔往里面看了一眼。如果这是当便桶用的，那一定很久没人清理过了。

source: I already know what's in that bucket. I'm not looking again.
target: 我已经知道那桶里是什么了。我才不要再看一遍。

source: That's Prince Fortinbras's bucket now.
target: 那现在是福丁布拉斯王子的桶了。

source: Lord Fortinbras is in there.
target: 福丁布拉斯大人在里面。

source: But shall not remain so.
target: 但我不会一直待在这里。

source: Oh? And what makes you so certain of that?
target: 哦？你凭什么这么肯定？

source: I'd be a poor tactician if I disclosed my every possible move.
target: 要是把所有可能的行动都透露出去，我这个谋略家也太不称职了。

source: I don't believe I've ever formally made your acquaintance, though by the look of you I know you are that Lady Ophelia.
target: 我想我们还没有正式结识过，不过看你的模样，我知道你就是那位奥菲莉娅女士。

source: If you expect me to have pleasantries to exchange with you, I don't. You're trying to burn my country to the ground.
target: 如果你指望我跟你寒暄，那就别想了。你正打算把我的国家烧成灰烬。

source: How unfortunate that this is your perception of my mission.
target: 你竟然这样看待我的使命，真是遗憾。

source: The Danish are like neglected dogs, snarling at anything unfamiliar. They have not known the touch of a kind master.
target: 丹麦人就像无人照料的狗，遇到任何陌生事物都会龇牙咆哮。他们从没得到过仁慈主人的抚慰。

source: When I am ruler of Denmark, allow me then to show you what such a kind touch looks like.
target: 等我统治丹麦时，就让我向你展示，这样仁慈的抚慰究竟是什么样的。

source: You keep away from my daughter! I may be a weak, sick old man, but there's strength in these bones enough to strangle you yet, Norway.
target: 离我女儿远点！我或许是个体弱多病的老头，但这把老骨头还有力气掐死你，挪威人。

source: Hmm. No need for that. I suspect the lady is capable of defending her own honor.
target: 嗯。没这个必要。我想这位女士有能力捍卫自己的名誉。

source: Ruler of Denmark is quite a leap for you in the present moment. For now, the only thing you're ruling is this cell. Farewell, and enjoy it.
target: 就你现在的处境，离统治丹麦可差得远呢。眼下你能统治的只有这间牢房。告辞，好好享受吧。

source: Yes, farewell. For now.
target: 好，告辞。暂且如此。

source: Still lingering?
target: 还没走？

source: Hardly.
target: 才不是。

source: I'm not a monster, Lady Ophelia. No more so, at least, than any of the men in this dour place.
target: 我不是怪物，奥菲莉娅女士。至少，我并不比这个阴沉地方的任何男人更像怪物。

source: Hmm.
target: 嗯。

source: Father.
target: 父亲。

source: It's my fault you're here.
target: 你被关在这里，都怪我。

source: Don't say that, my love. My faults and my actions are my own. It is by my hand that I am here.
target: 别这么说，亲爱的。我的过错和所作所为，都该由我自己负责。是我亲手让自己落到了这里。

source: (By your hand, perhaps, but I'm the one who tipped that hand.)
target: （也许是你亲手造成的，但推了你一把的人是我。）

source: The cell door is locked at the moment.
target: 牢门现在锁着。

source: Lady Ophelia, while I ordinarily respect your particular habit of, er, rummaging...
target: 奥菲莉娅女士，虽然我平时尊重你那个特别的习惯，呃，翻找东西……

source: Those are my personal belongings.
target: 但那些是我的私人物品。

source: Lady Ophelia, don' go gettin' in trouble wiv Bernardo!
target: 奥菲莉娅女士，别去招惹贝尔纳多啊！

source: He really dislikes it when yeh look through 'is things!
target: 他可讨厌别人翻他的东西了！

source: Las' time 'e caught me, I wos cleanin' boots until my hands got sores...
target: 上回被他逮到，我擦靴子擦得手都生疮了……

source: Let me see if I can find what Claudius asked Bernardo to hide. --Ah. This must be it.
target: 让我找找克劳狄斯让贝尔纳多藏起来的东西。——啊。一定就是这个。

source: Let me see if I can find what Claudius asked Bernardo to hide.—Ah. This must be it.
target: 让我找找克劳狄斯让贝尔纳多藏起来的东西。——啊。一定就是这个。

source: It's... a letter? And it looks like the seal's been broken, so I can't quite tell whose seal it is, but it's rather elaborate.
target: 这是……一封信？封印好像已经被拆开了，所以我看不太出那是谁的印章，不过样式倒是很精致。

source: This is horrible.
target: 这太可怕了。

source: I'm certain Gertrude must not yet know. What am I to do with this?
target: 我敢肯定，乔特鲁德一定还不知道。我该拿这封信怎么办？

source: And here's that letter again.
target: 又是那封信。

source: It looks like there's nothing else here at the moment, though.
target: 不过，这里目前好像没有别的东西了。

source: I fear you and I shall never be together, Mother.
target: 母亲，我怕我们永远也无法团聚了。

source: Father comes to visit her sometimes. Perhaps I should join him. He might like that.
target: 父亲有时会来看她。也许我该陪他一起来。他可能会喜欢这样。

source: The guards' quarters and our bedchambers are that way.
target: 卫兵住处和我们的卧室都在那边。

source: But I can't retire to my room until I find Laertes, like Father asked.
target: 不过，我得先按父亲的吩咐找到雷欧提斯，才能回房休息。

source: Nothing but the walls and the chapel this way.
target: 这边只有城墙和礼拜堂。

source: The King and Queen's private chambers are up that way. Laertes won't be up there.
target: 国王和王后的寝宫在那边楼上。雷欧提斯不会在那里。

source: My room isn't down that way.
target: 我的房间不在那边。

source: I'd better rest a while.
target: 我最好休息一会儿。

source: So little happened today, and yet my eyelids are already heavy.
target: 今天没发生多少事，可我的眼皮已经开始发沉了。

source: Maybe it's all the 'advice' I received.
target: 也许是因为听了太多“忠告”。

source: Father said Laertes was meeting with King Claudius.
target: 父亲说雷欧提斯正在会见克劳狄斯国王。

source: That way leads to the grounds outside Elsinore. They wouldn't be out there.
target: 那条路通往埃尔西诺城堡外的庭院。他们应该不会在那里。

source: Even in t his timeline, this bucket is still gross.
target: 就算在这条时间线里，这个桶还是那么恶心。

source: This bar's fireplace has a pleasent feel to it.
target: 这间酒馆的壁炉让人感觉很舒服。
